       w.precip_mm,
       w.wmo_code,
       COUNT(t.trip_id) AS trips_in_window
FROM investigator.nyc_daily_weather w
LEFT JOIN investigator.trips t
  ON t.pickup_date = w.day
 AND t.is_valid_trip
 AND t.pickup_hour BETWEEN 0 AND 13
WHERE w.day IN ('2024-07-31','2024-08-01')
GROUP BY w.day, w.precip_mm, w.wmo_code
ORDER BY w.day
json.why: This query applies the like-for-like window (pickup_hour BETWEEN 0 AND 13) to both focus days, ensuring a fair comparison of trip counts within the shared 14-hour period. By filtering to the same hour range on both Thursday and Wednesday, we eliminate the coverage bias where Thursday has only 14 hours of data versus Wednesday's full 24 hours. The LEFT JOIN preserves both days in the output even if one has zero trips, and GROUP BY day/precip/wmo_code isolates whether weather conditions differ between the two days while holding the time window constant. This directly tests Hypothesis H2: if Thursday shows significantly fewer trips than Wednesday within the identical 0–13 window, weather is a likely suppressor of demand.
